page: Amazon Web Services m7g.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the custom AWS Graviton processor family using the arm64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores running at 2.6 GHz with a Neoverse-V1 microarchitecture. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, and network connectivity is delivered via a 30 Gbps baseline interface managed by the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance and memory subsystem capabilities. The instance achieved a top-tier rating in Geekbench multi-core testing and software compilation with Clang, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score. Memory bandwidth is highly competitive, with read-only large block speeds reaching 253.34 GB/sec and write speeds at 121.49 GB/sec. Single-core performance across stress-ng and Geekbench remains in the average tier. In database and key-value store benchmarks, the instance demonstrated strong capabilities, processing 101.03 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and showing strong PassMark database performance.

From a resource density perspective, the ARM-based architecture provides an efficient hardware profile for multi-threaded workloads, though it lacks x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX or AMX. Large-scale LLM text generation shows mixed results, with strong performance on medium 7B models but poor throughput on smaller 135M models. Given the balanced memory-to-core ratio and strong multi-threaded execution, this instance is suited for software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and general-purpose containerized workloads.
